newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina accuses Israeli ambassador of interference.
newsitem.headline: Argentina accuses Israeli ambassador of interference.

text.p: Argentina's foreign ministry accused the Israeli ambassador on Thursday of interfering in national affairs after Ambassador Yitzhak Aviran complained about lack of arrests for desecrating a Jewish cemetery.
Vice Foreign Minister Andres Cisneros, in a press release, said statements by Aviran represented an "interference into the internal matters of Argentina."
The foreign ministry summoned the Isreali ambassador to express its upset at public statements made by him last weekend.
Aviran had said "there are degrees of tolerance beyond which when the culprits are not found, (a country's) political stability is affected."

He made the remarks following an attack on La Tablada, Argentina's largest Jewish cemetery, earlier this month in which 100 graves were desecrated. Gravestones were destroyed and others sprayed with large red swastikas.
Cisneros said both President Carlos Menem and Foreign Minister Guido di Tella were upset at the statements.
Cisneros told Aviran the remarks did not reflect the views of Isreal nor those of the Argentine Jewish community.

"The general picture of relations between Argentina and Israel are optimum and are surely at their most positive in the history of relations between the two countries," Cisneros said at the meeting with the ambassador, according to the press release.
"Ambassador Aviran's declarations do not express the respect nor the close communication of this bond between the two countries," added Cisneros.
In July 1994, a car bomb blew up the Jewish AMIA community centre in Buenos Aires, killing 86 people.

Argentina's Jewish community, one of the largest in the world, has suffered at least five cemetery desecrations in the last few years. In 1992 the Israeli Embassy was destroyed by a car bomb that killed 29 people.
Argentine security services have been criticised by the Jewish community, Israel and the United States for failing to find those responsible for the bomb attacks.
